The optimal asymptotic proportion is obtained by deleting all $S$‑smooth numbers whose total exponent sum is congruent to a fixed residue modulo $r\!+\!1$.  This hits every forbidden configuration $\{n,p_1n,\dots,p_rn\}$, leaving exactly $r$ of the $r+1$ residues, so a construction achieves density $r/(r+1)$.  Conversely, any subset avoiding such a configuration must miss at least one element of each $(r+1)$‑tuple, yielding the same upper bound.  Hence the limit exists and equals $r/(r+1)$.

**ANSWER:** $\displaystyle \frac{r}{\,r+1\,}$
